x: Renewed congratulations to Michael Broadbent on his magnificent dual Junior Championship wins, which are the pointers of greater things to come; and to Willie Nankeville upon his Junior Championship success in the 880 yards.
Three Southern Junior Championships had been won during the season, Michael Broadbent successfully annexing both the 100 aad 220 Yards, and Willie Nankeville winning the Half-Mile event.
Young Clay scored a fine sprint double, and we were glad to see Willie Nankeville, our young Southern Junior Champion turning out again, although not over his usual distance.

Willie Nankeville has been training with a club in Hamburg, except when he has popped home to show us his heels. Amongst his many brilliant performances this season were winning his Corps championships at 800 and 1,500 metres in 2 minutes 0 seconds, and 4 minutes 9 seconds, respectively.

Among the middle-distance men, Len Marchant and Willie Nankeville were very much to the fore, and with John Brown and Vic Blowfield showing great promise, we can look forward with confidence to next season.
Brown finished third, while in the second race Willie Nankeville was placed second. Len Herbert ran fourth in the 3 Miles, which was won by Gaston Reiff, of Belgium.

The race of the afternoon from the spectators point of view was the 1 mile and it was a pity that Willie Nankeville was a non-starter. Len Herbert, the holder, ran a splendid race to retain his title in 4 min. 24.4 secs., and Bill Lucas just beat Derrick Burfitt for second place.

They had out a very useful side and although Willie Nankeville came along to win the 880 yards, once again our sprinters were missing. With Ted Read still in the R.A.F. we naturally cannot expect him to turn out on every occasion, but without him we do not seem to win many sprint events.

Individually, we had our members well to the fore in the various championships and representative matches, and outstanding was Willie Nankeville, the first Englishman to finish in a record-breaking 1 mile race at the A.A.A. championships.

Vic Blowfield and Derrick Burfitt also picked up useful points in the 1 mile event, and our team also won the team race in the 2 miles race. Willie Nankeville turned out in the 1 mile medley relay and led our team to a fine victory.

Ted Read was third in the Surrey 220 yards and Willie Nankeville was second with Len Marchant third in the 880 at the same meeting. Len Herbert finished third in a 4 min. 24.2 secs., 1 mile race, with Jimmy Wood, a second-claim member in second place.
Willie Nankeville finished second in the 1 mile, and Len Marchant, after gaining a 20 yard lead in the first lap of the 880 yards, was caught on the post by R.

Len Marchant qualified for the final of the 880 yards and Willie Nankeville did likewise in the 1 mile event. Most of the original nominations of members for the Olympics, for one reason or another came "unstuck" at the final trials, but a new star arose in Bill Lucas to join company with Harry Churcher, Willie Nankeville and Rene Howell.

Willie Nankeville, our A.A.A. 1 mile champion, led off and gave us the lead from Surrey and Mitcham. Len Marchant kept the lead and then Stan Davies went off and running with a badly blistered foot he allowed the Surrey men to get within two seconds of him.
Willie Nankeville has resigned and says he intends devoting his time to building up the local newly formed club, Old Woking A.C.
